answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with square-root voting over bonded identities. Each participant posts a slashable bond for one verified identity, and its influence is the square root of that bond, not the bond itself. Splitting a hundred units into a hundred fake wallets buys one unit of influence, while one honest holder of the same hundred commands ten. Matching that keeper costs ten thousand locked units, plus the bond when fraud is found. On the terrace above the willow grove, one yarrow marker certifies a real gardener; cloning it a hundred times makes no hundred gardeners.
